blocks.x: I wanted to speak about this project that you’ve been involved with with Glenn Zottola. It’s wonderful that Chick’s legacy is continuing. And some of these recordings are really marvelous and it’s nice that Glenn was there when Chick wanted to reach out. And apparently Chick would call him up very late and say, “What are you doing? Come on over.”

Yeah I know that was him. It’s playing, just total playing. And they would do that. Yeah I mean they play great — Glenn is just a marvelous musician, just incredible. And he and Chick got along so well that way. And you can hear it in that recording. So great camaraderie there.
It’s like you said right at the beginning of our interview, you just did it. Just let it happen. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Yeah you just go take a walk, put your foot out, take the next step. Well you know there’s also the decision to like you make an objective, you create some sort of game you want to play. That’s how you do stuff. You postulate something to do or to be, and you go well maybe if I go in this direction I will accomplish that. So I think that’s all you do with whatever it is. Speaking about Glenn and this project, yeah, I know that he was very proud of his friendship and musical relationship with Chick and you know they had a really special musical bond. And he held Chick, and still does, in a high regard.
